## Slides

Each session ships a standalone reveal.js deck with the same content as the
corresponding chapters. The slides open full-screen in your browser: use the
arrow keys (or the on-screen controls) to navigate, `F` for full-screen and `S`
for the presenter notes — the notes include what to say and where to pause.

## Session 1 — module setup, track choice, AI policy

[Open the Session 1 slides](slides/2026-08-26-seance-1-slides.html)

- Structure of the module, technical program and calendar.
- The survey run in session and how it shapes the course.
- Track A / Track B choice and the AI use policy.

## Session 2 — designing an AI tutor: principles & demo

[Open the Session 2 slides](slides/2026-08-27-seance-2-slides.html)

- Returns the survey results from the room: equipment, existing usage, and how
  students feel about large language models.
- Why a *configured* tutor beats a plain model — system prompt, syllabus.
- Two prompts side by side, a live demo, and how to spot a false (or harmful)
  answer.

## Session 3 — designing an AI tutor: the prompt workshop

[Open the Session 3 slides](slides/2026-09-01-seance-3-slides.html)

- Write your v1 tutor *system prompt* from the six-block anatomy of Session 2 —
  role, method, anti-cheating, hallucinations, tone & format, context.
- Test it on three typical questions, a fresh session each.
- Iterate to a v2, peer-review in pairs, and deposit your v1 before Session 4.

## Session 4 — learning plan & contract

[Open the Session 4 slides](slides/2026-09-03-seance-4-slides.html)

- The five-section learning plan: objectives per module, sequencing, success criteria
  & evidence, follow-up schedule, and the contract.
- The fill-in template, classic mistakes to avoid, and how the plan counts in your
  assessment.
- Write your plan v0 in class and deposit it before Session 5, where it is validated.

## Session 5 — learning plan validation (walk-through)

[Open the Session 5 slides](slides/2026-09-22-seance-5-slides.html)

- You present your learning plan in a short pitch (~5 min) while the instructor circulates
  in the room.
- Three questions: where you are stuck, the hardest objective you wrote, when and how you
  will prove it.
- Verdict on the spot: validated, or a short list of adjustments. Anyone not seen during
  the session validates asynchronously before Friday.

## Session 6 — first follow-up (M1–M2)

[Open the Session 6 slides](slides/2026-09-28-seance-6-slides.html)

- First check-in on autonomous work: M1 (async) and M2 (IPC & locks).
- A quick common mini-review, then the four classic pitfalls (GIL, deadlock, blocking the
  event loop, fork vs spawn).
- Rotating stand-ups (~5 min per group) while the rest works, and the first logbook check.
